newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 30.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wenesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The release of U.S. economic data which eased inflation worries caused stocks and bonds to surge.

* According to papers filed in a suit in a state court, management at GTE's California subsidiary instructed workers to shred documents related to a regulatory probe into allegedly fraudulent billing practices.
* IBM announced a $3.5 billion share buyback program and a 14 percent dividend boost.
* PepsiCo's first quarter profits rose 8.4 percent and the stock price gained 10 percent.
* Union Pacific announced plans to join a consortium bidding for a busy Mexican rail line.
* Fund and brokerage firms said in April, mutual fund investors started to slowly come back into the market.
* Occidental Petroleum's president acknowledged the company increased its revenue through money-losing crude-oil trading to make its natural gas and oil business look larger.
* Cigarette display racks' future hinges on if they are seen as advertising or a way to give children access to tobacco.
* A $5.3 million jury verdict against Digital Equipment in a keyboard injury case was thrown out in the face of new evidence which indicated the plaintiff's problem was not related to work.
* Boeing was named the main contractor for Teledesic's planned $9 billion satellite-communications network.
* Television Azteca said it would look to prevent General Electric unit NBC from exercising a right to purchase up to 10 percent of Azteca.
* Tele-Communications said it would report strong cash flow growth and a slight revenue increase in the first quarter.
* Oracle Chairman Lawrence Ellison said he would put off pursuing a takeover bid for Apple Computer for the moment.

* Heard on the Street: A lot of brokerage firms have buy lists, priority lists, lists of stocks to buy now, even lists of their analysts' single best ideas. Now Goldman Sachs has come up with what you might call a Losers List.
* Credit markets: The Treasury market embraced friendly inflation data to stage a broad rally.
